title: VoiceInk vs. Wispr Flow (Oct 2026)
summary: Which dictation app wins in October 2026, VoiceInk or Wispr Flow? Compare speed, accuracy, pricing, and team support before you decide.
body_markdown:
The[VoiceInk vs Wispr Flow](https://willowvoice.com/) comparison comes down to two tools that share a category but not much else, plus a third that closes the gaps both leave open. VoiceInk is a Mac-first app with local processing and a flat fee, with an iOS companion still in beta, while Wispr Flow runs in the cloud across Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android with command-driven editing. Both carry real tradeoffs, and for some workflows, neither one is the right answer.


**TLDR:**


-


VoiceInk is Mac-first (Apple Silicon only, with an iOS companion app in beta) and runs at roughly 2 seconds of latency in Willow's testing. It publishes no shared dictionaries, admin controls, or compliance certifications.


-


Wispr Flow runs on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android at around 900ms at average dictation length in Willow's September 2026 benchmarking. Its Pro plan adds a shared dictionary and team usage analytics, and its Growth plan adds SSO and admin tools.


-


Wispr Flow provides a SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 certificate through its Trust Center and supports HIPAA workflows with a signed BAA on Growth and Enterprise plans. That makes it the stronger compliance choice of the two, though those controls sit on higher-priced tiers.


-


VoiceInk requires manual configuration for specialized terminology like client names, medical terms, or internal jargon and does not adapt automatically. Wispr Flow's Free plan includes a dictionary and learns names and jargon, though it caps dictation at 2,000 words per week on desktop.


-


A third tool covered below runs natively on Mac, Windows, and iOS at around 200ms with 98%+ accuracy. It adds shared team dictionaries and admin controls on its Team plan, SOC 2 Type II compliance and zero data retention on every plan, and a free plan with no word cap and no credit card required.


**Willow Voice is the better pick over both VoiceInk and Wispr Flow for professional and team workflows, processing at ~200ms with 98%+ accuracy, SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance with zero data retention on every plan, and shared team dictionaries and admin controls on the Team plan.**


## What Is VoiceInk?


VoiceInk is a[Mac-first voice dictation app](https://tryvoiceink.com/) built around local processing and a one-time payment ([$25 to $49 lifetime](https://tryvoiceink.com/pricing) ), a detail worth comparing against[Willow Voice vs Wispr Flow](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/wisprflow) . It is open source, requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14.4 or later, and has an iOS companion app that is still in beta. With local models, no audio leaves your device and there is no monthly bill, which appeals to privacy-conscious users who want to avoid recurring fees.


The tradeoffs are structural. Formatting depends on manual configuration through enhancement prompts and model or API key setup, and VoiceInk publishes[no team features](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/voiceink) , shared dictionaries, or admin controls, and no enterprise compliance credentials such as SOC 2 or HIPAA. It's built for one person and their own Macs.


## What Is Wispr Flow?


Wispr Flow is a cloud-based AI dictation tool built for individual professionals who want voice input across any app without switching windows. It runs on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, and uses a command-driven approach: speak your content, then issue instructions like "make this more formal" to reshape output. In Willow's September 2026 benchmarking, transcription latency runs around 900ms at average dictation length (400ms for short clips, 700ms for long ones) on its Electron-based architecture.


On compliance,[Wispr Flow](https://wisprflow.ai/) 's Trust Center provides a[SOC 2 Type II](https://trust.wispr.ai/) report and an ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate. HIPAA workflows run through a[signed BAA](https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/3467817258-security-and-compliance-faq) managed by Growth and Enterprise admins. The[Wispr Flow free plan](https://willowvoice.com/blog/wispr-flow-free-plan-alternatives) caps at 2,000 words per week on desktop and 1,000 words per week on mobile. Pro runs $15 per user per month billed monthly, or $12 per user per month billed annually, and includes unlimited dictation, a shared dictionary and snippets, shared team workspace, centralized billing, and team usage analytics. Growth runs $23 per month billed monthly, or $18 billed annually, and adds SAML SSO, org-wide HIPAA enforcement with a signed BAA, and admin tools. Enterprise pricing is custom. Confirm current pricing at wisprflow.ai/pricing before purchasing.

VoiceInk is a Mac app, with[no VoiceInk for Windows](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/voiceink) version and an iOS companion app still in beta, so organizations running Windows desktops alongside Mac laptops cannot cover the fleet with it. Wispr Flow supports Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, covering more ground for individuals and teams mixing devices.


Willow Voice runs natively on Mac, Windows, and iOS with full feature parity and no beta caveats. For mixed-device teams running Windows workstations, Mac laptops, and iPhones, one rollout covers the entire fleet without per-device reconfiguration.


## Latency and Speed Compared


Willow Voice processes at ~200ms across all dictation lengths, holding flat whether you speak for five seconds or five minutes. There is no perceptible wait between finishing a sentence and seeing it on screen.


VoiceInk's local processing runs around 2 seconds in Willow's testing on Apple Silicon, and slower on older hardware, and it depends on the model chosen. Wispr Flow runs at 400ms on short clips, around 900ms at average length, and 700ms on long dictations, per Willow's September 2026 benchmarking.


## Accuracy and Personalization Compared


In Willow's September 2026 benchmark measuring zero-edit rate (output correct with no edits needed), Willow Voice scored 95% in English against Wispr Flow's 90%. See the[zero-edit rate benchmark across 10 languages](https://willowvoice.com/blog/dictation-accuracy-zero-edit-rate-benchmark) for the full set of results. Willow Voice separately reports 98%+ accuracy in English based on its own internal benchmarking; Wispr Flow's own materials may report different figures for its accuracy. VoiceInk's site claims near-perfect accuracy with local models but publishes no benchmark to confirm it, so real-world results depend on the model you choose and your hardware. Context-specific behavior in VoiceInk depends on manual configuration rather than any built-in awareness.


The gap goes beyond the numbers. VoiceInk's accuracy depends entirely on your hardware and manually configured enhancement prompts, and it does not adapt automatically. Wispr Flow improves output through post-dictation commands, and its Free plan lists personalization that learns names and jargon through a dictionary and snippets.


Willow's Auto-Dictionary handles this automatically. Correct a term a few times and it gets added to your personal dictionary permanently, and the context-aware engine reads your active application to handle specialized vocabulary correctly from the start.


## AI Writing Features Compared


VoiceInk offers optional AI enhancement that cleans up filler words and reformats what you dictated into emails or notes, and it can rewrite selected text from a spoken instruction. Using this requires configuring models or API keys, and its published features do not describe reading an email thread to draft a context-aware reply from a spoken prompt.


Wispr Flow goes a step further with a command layer: after recording your voice input, you can issue instructions like "make this shorter" or "rewrite formally" to reshape output. That is still a two-step process, and neither tool's published features describe reading an existing email thread and generating a context-aware reply from a spoken prompt.


Willow Scribe does. Speak a prompt like "write a follow-up to Sarah about the proposal timeline" and it generates a complete, ready-to-send message in one step, with no typing required. It can also read the conversation thread your cursor is in and produce a reply that matches the context already set.


For high-volume communication workflows, that distinction is the one that matters. Transcription helps you type faster. Generation removes the composition step entirely.


## Team and Enterprise Features Compared


VoiceInk publishes no shared dictionaries, no SSO, and no admin console. Licenses are sold per person, with one license covering one to three of that person's Macs. If ten people at a company want to use it, each person configures their own setup independently.


Wispr Flow's compliance posture is genuinely strong: its Trust Center provides a SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate, and HIPAA workflows run through a signed BAA on Growth and Enterprise. For individual professionals in[compliance-sensitive teams](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-voice-dictation-for-enterprise-teams) , that coverage is meaningful. Wispr Flow's Pro plan already includes a shared dictionary, shared team workspace, centralized billing and user management, and team usage analytics. Growth adds SAML SSO, admin tools, and org-wide HIPAA enforcement, and Enterprise adds SCIM, audit logs, and managed deployment. Willow Voice, by comparison, applies SOC 2 Type II compliance and zero data retention on every plan, while shared dictionaries and admin controls come with the Team plan at $10/user/month billed annually, and a signed BAA is available at Enterprise.


Willow Voice is built for org-wide deployment. Shared custom dictionaries let teams standardize terminology once and deploy it across every member's device without per-user setup. SOC 2 Type II compliance and zero data retention apply on every plan, while shared dictionaries and admin controls that push vocabulary changes across the group come with the Team plan at $10/user/month billed annually, and a signed BAA is available at Enterprise. For mixed-device organizations running Windows workstations, Mac laptops, and iPhones in the same fleet, vocabulary and settings carry across every device automatically.

Wispr Flow's free tier caps at roughly 2,000 words per week on desktop and 1,000 words per week on mobile, which runs out fast for anyone using voice as a primary input method. The Pro plan runs $12 per user per month billed annually ($15 billed monthly) and includes unlimited dictation plus a shared dictionary and team workspace. The Growth plan runs $18 per user per month billed annually ($23 billed monthly) and adds SSO and a signed BAA. Worth noting plainly: Wispr Flow's Pro price lands at the same $12 per month as Willow Voice's Individual plan, while Willow Voice's Team plan runs $10 per user per month billed annually. Confirm current prices directly on each vendor's site before purchasing, as these figures change.


Willow Voice's paid Individual plan delivers faster, more accurate dictation plus unlimited Willow Scribe at $12 per month billed annually. The Team plan at $10 per user per month adds shared custom dictionaries deployed org-wide and admin controls for pushing vocabulary changes without touching individual installs. For teams evaluating before committing, the free plan offers unlimited AI dictation with no word cap and no credit card required.


## Why Willow Voice Is the Better Choice


Willow Voice closes both gaps without asking you to pick which limitation to live with.


For team contexts, shared custom dictionaries let engineering, legal, healthcare, and finance teams standardize terminology org-wide from day one, with no per-user setup, supporting[sales and team workflows](https://willowvoice.com/blog/willow-wispr-flow-sales-team-comparison) alike. Admin controls push vocabulary changes across the whole group without touching individual installs. SOC 2 Type II compliance and zero data retention are built into the product on every plan, shared dictionaries and admin controls come with the Team plan, and a signed BAA is available at the Enterprise tier for clinical and compliance-sensitive workflows. For mixed-device organizations, vocabulary and settings carry across Mac, Windows, and iOS automatically, so a developer on a Windows workstation and a colleague on a MacBook work from the same setup.


For individual use, the ~200ms latency holds flat across short clips and long dictations alike, and the 98%+ accuracy means output lands clean by default. The Auto-Dictionary builds your personal vocabulary automatically from corrections, and Willow Scribe generates complete messages from a spoken prompt instead of transcribing word for word, a capability neither VoiceInk nor Wispr Flow supports.


## FAQs


### Which is more accurate, VoiceInk or Wispr Flow?


Only Wispr Flow has a benchmark result to compare: a 90% English zero-edit rate in Willow's September 2026 benchmarking, against 95% for Willow Voice. VoiceInk was not part of that benchmark and publishes no accuracy figure, so its results depend on the local model you choose and your hardware.


### Is VoiceInk good for teams?


Not well. VoiceInk is licensed per person and publishes no shared dictionaries, admin controls, or compliance certifications, so each user configures their own setup independently.


### Does Wispr Flow work on Windows?


Yes. Wispr Flow dictation runs on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android. Its Notetaker add-on currently supports Mac and Windows only.


### Which tool has lower latency, VoiceInk or Wispr Flow?


Wispr Flow runs about 400ms on short clips, around 900ms at average length, and 700ms on long dictations in Willow's September 2026 benchmarking. VoiceInk's local processing takes approximately 2 seconds in Willow's testing, with slower results on older hardware. Neither matches Willow Voice's ~200ms.


### What is a better alternative to both VoiceInk and Wispr Flow?


Willow Voice is a[better alternative to both](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/alternatives) tools. It runs natively on Mac, Windows, and iOS with ~200ms latency, 98%+ accuracy, and an Auto-Dictionary that builds your personal vocabulary automatically. For teams, shared custom dictionaries and admin controls come with the Team plan, SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance with zero data retention apply on every plan, and the free plan is unlimited with no word cap and no credit card required.


## Final Thoughts on VoiceInk vs Wispr Flow


The[VoiceInk vs Wispr Flow](https://willowvoice.com/) decision is less about which tool wins and more about which constraint you can live with: Mac-first local processing, or cloud-based multi-device access with a weekly word cap on the free tier. Both tools work for individuals willing to configure them. If your needs include team vocabulary, compliance that applies on every plan, or generating a full message from a spoken prompt instead of transcribing one word at a time, Willow Voice is worth trying for free before you commit to either.
